data.title: Narrative Designed to Divide an Internal Audience
data.summary:
Campaign content works an existing internal division — between sites, functions or
staff groups — rather than attacking the organisation as a whole. The framing invites
one group to see another as the problem.
data.description:
Dividing is cheaper than persuading. An operation that cannot change what an audience
believes about the organisation can still change what parts of the organisation believe
about each other, and that produces real operational damage: slower decisions, withheld
information, and staff who will not raise a concern because of who would receive it.

The content usually reads as sympathetic to whichever group is being addressed. That is
what makes it effective and what makes it hard for the organisation to respond — a
rebuttal addressed to everyone implicitly sides against someone.

Where the division worked on is genuine, say so. A report that treats a real grievance
purely as an adversary's talking point will be dismissed by the staff who hold it, and
the recommendation that follows from it will not be implemented.
data.recommendation:
* Address the underlying grievance through normal internal channels, separately from any
  response to the campaign; conflating the two discredits both.
* Avoid public rebuttals that require the organisation to take one internal side.
* Brief managers of the targeted groups directly, so that the first they hear of it is
  not from the campaign.
data.short_recommendation: Address the real grievance separately from the campaign response.

disarm_techniques.technique: T0083 — Integrate Target Audience Vulnerabilities into Narrative
